Problem: All three-digit numbers are written in a row: $100101102 \ldots 998999$. How many times in this row does a zero follow a two?

<reflection>
The row is the concatenation of all three-digit numbers from 100 to 999. The task is to count adjacent digit pairs '20' in this concatenation. Examples 120 and 202 show a '20' inside a number counts, whether in the last two digits or the first two digits.
This limits qualifying numbers to those with last two digits 20, but numbers with first two digits 20 (200-209) also contain a zero immediately following a two.
Count the disjoint cases where the first two digits are 20 and where the last two digits are 20, then add them.
</reflection>
